A CHAMBER RED THAT READS LIKE A PHASE FAILURE AND IS NOT ONE. Signature, so the next reader does not spend twenty minutes on it:

    regenerate-artifacts: done.                                   <- the phase SUCCEEDED
    scripts/timed.sh: line 75: /tmp/tmp.XXXXXXXX: No such file or directory
    scripts/timed.sh: line 77: user: unbound variable
    scripts/sluice-run.sh: line 371: /tmp/tmp.YYYYYYYY: No such file or directory
    sluice-run: PHASE artifacts FAILED — holding.

If you see "done." from the phase's own script immediately above an "unbound variable" from timed.sh, the work finished and the STOPWATCH died. The candidate is not implicated. campaign/the-warrant paid a serial-box slot and an attribution for this on 2026-09-06.

MECHANISM. timed.sh and sluice-run.sh each do `tmp=$(mktemp)`, run the command with `time` writing into it, then `read` it back. If the file is gone at read time the variables stay unset and `set -u` aborts on first expansion -- after the command has already exited 0.

WHAT DELETED THE FILES IS UNKNOWN, and I would rather leave that open than guess. Ruled out by command: /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/tmp.conf gives /tmp age `-`, i.e. NO aging, so systemd-tmpfiles cannot have done it and the daily timer is a red herring; no tmpwatch/tmpreaper cron; /tmp 34% full; journal silent for the window. NOT ruled out: a concurrent actor on the box running `rm -rf /tmp/tmp.*`. If you go looking, know that an empty ~/.bash_history proves nothing -- agent shells are non-interactive and write no history, so that check is weaker than it appears. Two different tempfiles in two different scripts vanishing inside one 290 s window is one actor, not two coincidences.

FIXED at 620475046 (tooling/timing-must-not-veto-the-phase, not yet landed): an unreadable timing is now a missing row and an stderr notice, never a failed command. Deliberately not a `?` row -- that would break the census-duration reader.

THE GENERAL RULE, which is the part worth keeping: A MEASUREMENT MUST NOT HOLD VETO POWER OVER THE THING IT MEASURES. Instrumentation is the least important thing in any pipeline it sits in, and `set -u` quietly promotes an absent measurement into a failed assertion. If you wrap anything in a timer, a counter or a profiler, check what happens when the instrument alone fails.

AND A SMALLER ONE, paid for on the way: timed.sh hardcoded docs/timings.md, so writing a test for it appended real rows to a TRACKED file, and cleaning up with `git checkout -- docs/timings.md` destroyed a carried measurement row too. Same trap scripts/CLAUDE.md documents for mutate.py. A test that needs cleanup in a tracked file wants a path seam instead; there is now HV_TIMINGS_LEDGER, and it is a test seam only.
